data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note summarizes results from the Survey of Adult Skills 2023 for England (United Kingdom) using adults aged 16–65 assessed in 2022–23. The survey measures three domains—literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving—via a personal interview plus a self-completed digital assessment on tablets, with proficiency reported on 500-point scales and mapped to discrete proficiency levels. England’s mean proficiency is above the OECD average in all three domains (literacy 272, numeracy 268, adaptive problem solving 259), with shares at low proficiency (e.g., 18% at Level 1 or below in literacy) and high proficiency (e.g., 14% at Levels 4–5 in literacy). The note also reports descriptive comparisons by age and education, and associations between numeracy proficiency and labour force participation, unemployment risk, and wages, as well as links to well-being and civic outcomes, while noting that doorstep respondents are excluded in cross-cycle comparisons. No student-level machine learning model, PV strategy, or missing-data procedure is described in the excerpt, so the methodological details required for ML replication are not available here.
